text: A dog comes back from a hunting trip in the Swiss Alps, covered in burrs. They cling to its fur and won't let go. <#0.4#> Its owner, an engineer named George de Mestral, wondered: why do they stick so well? <#0.5#> So he looked at a burr under a microscope. <#0.3#> It was covered in hundreds of tiny hooks. <#0.4#> And each hook caught on anything with a loop. Fur, hair, even the threads in his clothes. <#0.5#> So George thought: what if we made that? One strip of hooks. One strip of loops. <#0.5#> It took him about ten years to get right. He called it Velcro, from the French words for velvet and hook. <#0.4#> Today it holds shoes, bags, and even astronauts' gear in space. All thanks to one very sticky dog.
